topic: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
usual_baseline: Time to surgery is the hardest standard. Surgery within 36 hours was 39.6–48.3% [1535, 1491]; best practice tariff met in 28–44.4% [1535, 1526]. Orthogeriatric review is often late (mean 91 hours [1543]) or rare (11% [1766]). Delays are mainly for medical review or theatre space [1453, 1488]. Bone health and falls assessment lag.
fix_that_works: Whole pathway redesign with orthogeriatricians: surgery within 36 hours 39.6% to 84%, tariff 28% to 83%, 30-day mortality 7.8% to 5.3% [1535]. A joint admission pathway: mortality 14% to 4% [1543]. A clerking booklet and orthogeriatric rounds: tariff 44.4% to 91.7% [1526]. A national database with dashboards: geriatrician assessment 11% to 86% [1766].
fix_that_fails: Stopping continuous audit: surgery within 48 hours fell from 98.4% to 91.8% and ED waits worsened until it restarted [1519]. Benchmarking and teaching lifted nerve blocks only from 8.0% to 25.4% [1699]. Circulating results left function and mortality unchanged [1415]. National tariff compliance rose only 7% to 21% [1766].
consultant_advice: The national database already measures this every month; a local repeat adds little. Audit one breach cause, such as delay for medical review, or an unmeasured item like nerve block in ED. Gains fade when audit stops, so plan to keep measuring.
